svg.text: AURALYNK · ARCHITECTURE 06
Validation Evidence
Three different kinds of proof — each answers a different question.
LEVEL 1
DSP UNIT / DETERMINISTIC TESTS
Environment: Node.js, no browser, no audio hardware.
Runs the real TypeScript sources through the Vite SSR loader —
the exact code that ships in the browser.
CRC-16 known answers · framing round trips · corruption and
truncation · modulate → demodulate end to end at several sample
rates, chunk sizes and symbol phases · AWGN at 20 dB and 12 dB ·
clock drift ±0.1 % and ±0.3 % · 60 / 60 checks passing.
Answers: "is the DSP algorithm correct and robust?"
LEVEL 2
BROWSER / AUTOMATED E2E
Environment: production bundle served by Vite, loaded in Chrome.
Page loads · application mounts · Auralynk branding and favicon
resolve · transmitter, receiver, Signal Lab, calibration and
architecture sections render · zero console errors · zero failed
network requests.
Answers: "does the built application actually run in a browser?"
LEVEL 3
REAL SPEAKER → AIR → MICROPHONE
Environment: physical hardware, real room, no signal injection.
Message "Hello from Auralynk." · F0 15,000 Hz · F1 16,500 Hz ·
20 ms symbols · 48,000 Hz microphone · 224 symbols · 4480 ms.
Result: decoded message matched, CRC OK (verified 2026-10-07).
Answers: "does the system survive a real acoustic channel?"
These layers are not interchangeable: passing level 1 or 2 never substitutes for a physical acoustic test.
